questions.q: What problem does a server environment solve?
options: Scheduling a package to run at a specific time
Encrypting the SSISDB database at rest
Automatically converting packages to the project deployment model
Running the same deployed project with different runtime values (like connection strings) depending on where it executes
questions.explain: An environment is a named container of variables (Dev, Test, Production) that lets one deployed project pull different runtime values depending on which environment reference is used for a given execution.

questions.q: Where do you create a new environment in Object Explorer?
options: Right-click SQL Server Agent and select New Job
Right-click the SSISDB database node and select Create Catalog
Right-click the package itself and select Execute
Right-click the Environments folder under your folder in SSISDB and select Create Environment
questions.explain: Environments live in the Environments folder alongside Projects, inside a folder under SSISDB — right-click it and choose Create Environment.

questions.q: What must you add to a project before you can map its parameters to variables in a specific environment?
options: A second copy of the project deployed to a different folder
Nothing — parameters map to environments automatically on deployment
An environment reference, added on the project's References page via Configure
A new SQL Server Agent job step
questions.explain: You right-click the project, select Configure, and on the References page add a reference to the environment — that's what makes its variables available for mapping.

questions.q: How do you map a specific parameter to an environment variable's value?
options: Set the parameter's default value in SSDT before deploying
On the Parameters tab, browse the parameter's Value field, select "Use environment variable," and choose the variable
Edit the .ispac file directly in a text editor
Rename the parameter to exactly match the variable's name
questions.explain: The parameter and variable names don't need to match — mapping is explicit: browse the Value field, choose "Use environment variable," and select which variable feeds that parameter.

questions.q: What is the one hard rule about environments and a single package execution?
options: Environment variables can never be marked Sensitive
A single execution can pull variable values from only one referenced environment, never a mix of two
An environment can only contain one variable
A project can have at most one environment reference total
questions.explain: Even if a project references multiple environments, any one execution must specify exactly one of them — mixing variables from two environments in a single run isn't possible.
